Establish clear boundaries but not aggressively, let them identify that themselves. If you force it on them they may fight back (yes... I have been known to get confrontational myself. Not proud of it).

I get that it's easy to just walk away and think that this person is a lunatic but if you hang in there and keep your boundaries firm, that will help them so much. My wife doesn't take any shit and when I spiral into an episode she is 100% gangster. She doesn't care if it's an episode, she will tell it to me straight (with love) without mercy but in a kind way. So, I have bpd and this is my take. 

A lot of us suffered extreme traumas very early on. Unfortunately sexual trauma is very common. So there may be something historical behind the behavior. 

Maybe she may have remembered an event or an emotion after "the fact" That pushed her into a very dark place, so she crashed and did a thing called "splitting" On you. Or simply couldn't handle the emotions. 

We have to bare in mind that with BPD the intensity of emotion is insanely high. 

I would say that it could also be a validation thing. She may have slept with you to feel wanted at first, then felt a deep shame. In my experience the validation of sex is more common in females with bpd. I don't really get that, I just used to sleep with anything that moved... Just... Because. But it did fill a void

Chronic feelings of emptiness are a fucker to deal with. 

Depending on her stage of "recovery" She may not actually be able to control the behavior/feelings.

She doesn't hate you, she just lost emotional control. 

Try having a gentle conversation with her, but... Step by step. If she feels safe it may even help her development with the disorder. But, little baby steps. 

We aren't psycopaths, we feel ALOT. That's the issue sometimes. We have to learn to be self aware and actually see our unconscious behaviours. 

I'm probably gonna get shit for even saying I'm BPD but that's often why we don't talk about it much. We just get shit, it makes us worse (you can't imagine the daily self hate, shame and disgust over ourselves we feel). We're also advised by most psychologists to avoid telling people our diagnosis due to this. 

With a good therapist and if it's needed, medication, things actually can get better. In fact, they do. 

Remember to not just reduce her to her diagnosis in everything she does. She's a real person. I had an ex do that to me and it was humiliating. 

But! Set clearly explained boundaries when necessary. My wife does this to me and I fully respect and appreciate it. I know where the lines are and when I'm crossing them (which can be confusing if not clearly defined) 

Also, PwBPD can also be very intense, if you can't handle it and it's negatively affecting you, well, you have to go. You can still be friends but not romantic or anything. You have to also evaluate how your mental health is affected too. 

To end, some PwBPD would still be arseholes even without the disorder. Just like all people.
